package_info.why_malicious: Vulnerable versions of Nexus Repository Manager 3 contain CVE-2019-7238, a remote code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server via crafted HTTP requests. While the package itself is not intentionally malicious, the presence of this vulnerability enables attackers to inject and execute malicious code, making affected versions dangerous if unpatched.

execution_context.file_location: REST API endpoint (vulnerable Java class in NXRM 3 core)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP POST request to the /service/rest/beta/repositories endpoint with a malicious payload that exploits a Java Expression Language (EL) injection vulnerability, such as: { "name": "test", "online": true, "storage": { "blobStoreName": "default", "strictContentTypeValidation": true }, "format": "maven2", "type": "hosted", "attributes": { "repository": { "content": "${''.getClass().forName('java.lang.Runtime').getRuntime().exec('touch /tmp/pwned')}" } } }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This payload exploits the Java EL injection vulnerability in the REST API, causing the server to execute arbitrary system commands (e.g., creating a file /tmp/pwned) when the payload is processed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary system commands on the server, which is a critical security risk.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal REST API usage should not allow arbitrary code execution or system command invocation via user-supplied input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for user-supplied data to be evaluated as Java code in this context.
key_indicators: User input evaluated as Java Expression Language (EL)
Ability to invoke java.lang.Runtime.exec() from API input
Creation of files or execution of commands not tied to normal repository operations

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious HTTP POST request exploiting the EL injection vulnerability in the REST API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the server (e.g., file creation, malware installation, data exfiltration)

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected system command execution triggered by REST API requests
Creation of files (e.g., /tmp/pwned) or processes not associated with normal repository operations
Unusual or malformed JSON payloads in POST requests to /service/rest/beta/repositories
file_indicators: Unexpected files or scripts appearing on the server after API requests
network_indicators: Unusual inbound POST requests to /service/rest/beta/repositories with suspicious JSON payloads
Outbound connections initiated by the server as a result of command execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor REST API endpoints for suspicious or malformed JSON payloads, especially those containing Java EL expressions or references to java.lang.Runtime. Audit server logs for unexpected file creation or process execution following API requests. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in the filesystem. Ensure all NXRM instances are updated to version 3.15 or later to prevent exploitation.
